moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Borrowed brilliance in a silver sky
moon.intro: To shine by reflected light is not a lesser act — it is an act of trust. The Moon receives and returns, asks nothing, keeps nothing. Its glow is not theft but devotion: a daily proof that receiving fully and giving completely can be the same gesture.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The wave forgets it is the sea
philosophy.intro: The wave rises, certain of its shape, proud of its height — then falls, astonished to find itself indistinguishable from the sea. The ego is this brief assertion of form over substance, a ripple that mistakes itself for the ocean. To dissolve is not to disappear but to return to what one always was.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Freedom beyond the fruit of action
gita.intro: The Gita was not spoken in a garden or a palace but on a field of war — where the stakes were absolute and every choice carried the weight of worlds. This is its radical claim: that the deepest wisdom does not require withdrawal from life but full immersion in it, with hands open and heart unguarded.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: The drum that speaks the universe
shiva.intro: Shiva does not dance for applause. The Tandava needs no audience because the audience is the dance — every atom, every star, every breath a movement in the choreography of becoming. Stillness and motion are not opposites here; they are the same gesture, seen from inside and outside the drum's resonance.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Light as the only subject
art.intro: A sunflower does not paint itself golden — it conspires with the sun, translating photons into pigment, light into living color. The impressionist knew this secret: that beauty is never static, never owned. It exists only in the meeting — between eye and object, between hand and canvas, between one fleeting moment and the next.
